cards.explanation: The answer is so they won't be defiled before the Passover. John says they stayed outside “…to avoid being defiled and unable to eat the Passover.” (John 18:28). So Pilate, the Roman governor, is the one who has to walk out to them. Think of a guest who won't come past the front mat, so the host ends up holding the whole conversation on the porch.

The answer is that He wouldn't be here if He weren't a criminal. They said, “If He were not a criminal, we would not have handed Him over to you.” Pilate asked for an accusation and they never named a crime. It's like asking a coworker why the meeting got moved and hearing "because it got moved." Round and round we go.

The answer is False. Pilate says, “You take Him and judge Him by your own law…” and they push back with, “We are not permitted to execute anyone…” (John 18:31). Nobody walks Jesus back out the door. The matter stays in Pilate's hands.

The answer is whether He is the King of the Jews. Pilate goes back in, summons Jesus, and asks, “Are You the King of the Jews?” (John 18:33). He doesn't open with small talk. Straight to the big question, no warm-up.
The answer is True. Pilate says, “Your own people and chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?” He starts by asking, “Am I a Jew?” So he's pointing at who brought Jesus to him.

The answers are world and fight. Jesus says, “My kingdom is not of this world…” and then adds, “if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews.” He says it again in different words at the end: “…My kingdom is not of this realm.” That tells us something about the kind of kingdom this is. His servants aren't swinging for Him in this room.

The answer is everyone who belongs to the truth. Jesus says, “Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice.” That comes right after He says He was born and came into the world to testify to the truth. It's a kingdom with a different kind of door.
The answer is True. Pilate goes out and tells them, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.” That's the first time he says it. It won't be the last, friends.
The answer is Barabbas. “Not this man…” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” John adds, “(Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist.)” Pilate offered them a choice and they picked someone else.

The answer is purple. John says the soldiers “…dressed Him in a purple robe.” (John 19:2). They twisted a crown of thorns and set it on His head too. I'll say only that this is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is Crucify Him. “As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, ‘Crucify Him! Crucify Him!’” It's right when they see Him. There's no waiting around. Pilate answers them, “You take Him and crucify Him…” (John 19:6).

The answer is that He declared Himself the Son of God. They say, “We have a law, and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.” And when Pilate hears it, he is even more afraid (John 19:8).
The answer is False. Pilate asks, “Where are You from?” and the text says, “But Jesus gave no answer.” It's quiet in that room. Pilate is left with his own question.

The answer is that it is given from above. Jesus says, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above.” Pilate had just listed his own authority. Jesus answers by telling him where it comes from.

The answer is the one who handed Him over to Pilate. Jesus says, “Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.” He says "to you," so He isn't pointing at Pilate. The text doesn't name who He means here.

The answer is True. The Jews keep shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar.” They add, “Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.” From then on, that's the pressure sitting on Pilate.

The answer is the judgment seat. Pilate “…sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.” So he's sitting officially now. John then says it was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate tells the Jews, “Here is your King!” (John 19:13-14).

The answer is that they have no king but Caesar. After Pilate asks, “Shall I crucify your King?” the chief priests answer, “We have no king but Caesar…” It's a short, flat answer, and then Pilate hands Jesus over (John 19:16).

The answer is False. Pilate said he found no basis for a charge against Him (John 19:4). He says it again in John 19:6: “I find no basis for a charge against Him.” Still, “…Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.” It's a hard place to stop, friends, and this story isn't over.
